column1: # NORMAN BASES -- M03 / M06 / Q02 on the double-perturbation composition benchmark
# WHAT WE ARE TRYING TO ACHIEVE OVERALL
# Predict a perturbation's effect in a context where that exact perturbation was never
# measured. Here the form is COMPOSITION: train on SINGLE-gene perturbations, predict PAIRS,
# where both genes were seen individually and the pair never was. Headline: split-half paired
# `pearson_delta` on the `additive` and `nonadditive` panels (36 pairs each), cell-eval 0.6.0,
# uncalibrated, 8,000-gene axis.
# WHAT THIS GRID ANSWERS
# Does any of the three designated bases learn something about composition that the additive
# baseline does not already have? `sum_of_singles` -- ctrl + delta_A + delta_B from the
# measured single arms -- IS this architecture's own operator in closed form, because
# `model.forward` sums the perturbations' graph embeddings. So this grid's real question is
# whether TRAINING adds anything over that closed form.
# WHAT IS VARIED / HELD FIXED
# VARIED: the loss composition (M03 balanced · M06 direction-dominated · Q02 = M06 + latent).
# HELD FIXED: the 150-epoch / eta_min 3e-4 schedule (F-sched3's best on rhj), batch 2048,
#   lr 1e-3, decoder_lr 1e-3, seed 42, adjacency_map + FiLM multiplicative_only + mean-free
#   (arm s313), and the singles-only corpus.
# ⚠️ THE WEIGHTS ARE RESCALED, NOT COPIED. Measured at init on both benchmarks with the same
# released encoder+decoder (scripts/norman/norman_loss_scale.py): smooth_l1 is 0.600x on
# norman, dcos 0.909x, delta_mag 0.204x, latent_mse 1.327x. `delta_mag` is 4.9x SMALLER here
# because the effect is larger relative to a control cell's own deviation, so copying
# 0.01363 across would have under-weighted it fivefold. The rescaling preserves each term's
# ratio TO smooth_l1 -- the ratio that defines the bases (M03 = dcos at parity, M06 = ~113x)
# -- not its absolute size.
#   rhj      -> norman
# ⚠️ ONE TRAINING PER BASE, NOT ONE PER COMPOSITION MODE. The 12 composition modes are
# INFERENCE strategies and are algebraically identical on a single perturbation, which is all
# training ever sees. So the same weights answer all 12 ways and the comparison is perfectly
# controlled (tests/test_composition_modes.py pins the identity).
# HOW TO READ THE RESULT -- PRE-REGISTERED
# any base > sum_of_singles on `additive` (0.8824) -> training adds something the closed form
#     lacks, on the pairs additivity already explains. The strongest possible claim.
# any base > sum_of_singles on `nonadditive` (0.7757) ONLY -> read with care: that panel is
#     drawn from sum_of_singles' own residual, so a margin there is partly selection.
# all three below the additive baseline -> Occam's summed-embedding composition is worse than
#     summing the measured deltas, i.e. the graph-embedding sum is the weak link, not the
#     data.
# M06/Q02 > M03 -> the direction-dominated regime transfers to composition too, as it does on
#     rhj. M03 > M06 -> it does not, and the base ranking is dataset-specific (F-latent4's
#     setup-dependence rule, one dataset further out).
# ANCHORS -- 5 splits, uncalibrated, additive / nonadditive
# sum_of_singles 0.8824 / 0.7757 · experimental 0.9165 / 0.8377 · meanpert 0.4634 / 0.4016
# mae (ERROR, lower better): sos 0.0126 / 0.0168 · experimental 0.0110 / 0.0129
# COST: the corpus is 47,269 single cells + 9,702 controls, ~12x smaller than rhj's 580k
# cells/epoch, so 150 epochs is minutes rather than hours. 3 arms.
# ⚠️ PREREQUISITE, and the run REFUSES without it: cache/pert_means/norman_2019_k562.npz
#     python scripts/pert_group_means.py --config configs/norman_combo.yaml
# `dcos` and `delta_mag` read that table; the gate stops the run rather than letting the
# terms evaluate to a silent zero (F-loss1). The first launch died on exactly this.
#   GRID=scripts/grids/norman_bases.tsv CONFIG=configs/norman_combo.yaml \
#   sbatch --qos=vco --wckey=vco --time=04:00:00 --array=0-2 scripts/slurm/rhj_loss_sweep.sbatch
# ⚠️ SIX ARMS, TWO SCHEDULES. `N*` run the schedule F-sched3 found best on rhj (150 epochs,
# eta_min 3e-4); `N*s` run the ORIGINAL 30-epoch / eta_min 1e-7 setup the three bases were
# defined at. On rhj the schedule was worth +0.0260 -- more than any loss term measured -- so
# whether that transfers to a different dataset AND a different task (composition) is its own
# question, and the 30-epoch arms are the only way to ask it here. They also make the Norman
# numbers directly comparable to the bases' published rhj numbers, which are 30-epoch.
# RHJ reference for the same contrast: Q02 30ep 0.3783 -> Y06 150ep/3e-4 0.4043 (+0.0260).
